name: Ossvin Ube-Tamarind Cream
manufacturer: Ossvin Foods (Corponation subsidiary — Halcyon Consumer Group)
description: A mass-produced cream soda from Halcyon's Ossvin line, combining synth-ube with synth-tamarind in a sweetened cream base. It's the affordable answer to the more expensive ube cream sodas in higher tiers — cheerfully artificial and unapologetic about it.
flavor_profile: Sweet synthetic ube — candy-purple and vanilla-adjacent — with a bright sour tamarind swirl through a thick cream base, finishing very sweet
slogan: Real flavor doesn't have to cost real money.
cultural_context: Ossvin Ube-Tamarind is comfort food in liquid form for Shelf and lower Tier 2 residents. Kids grow up on it. Adults buy it when they're stressed. There's no cultural cache to it — it's just deeply familiar, and familiarity in a hard city has its own value.
story_hooks: A Shelf community organizer has discovered that Ossvin's 'synth-tamarind' contains a trace appetite stimulant not listed on the ingredients — she's trying to get the information out without Halcyon's legal team burying it
A Tier 3 food nostalgia movement has ironically adopted Ossvin as a retro symbol of Shelf culture, commodifying it in ways that the Shelf residents who actually drink it find quietly infuriating
The Ossvin factory in the outer Shelf district is the largest employer in the area — a labor dispute there could destabilize the entire local economy, and both sides know it
